title: log
description:
Git repos are just a list of commits that represent the entire (yes, _entire_. The entire directory) at x point in time.
The `git log` command shows your git commit history. This is where the _version control_ part of the version control system comes in. It lets you see the who, when and what of each commit.

## Commit Hashes
Commits get a unique string to differentiate them. These are called commit hashes. A commit hash is typically a very long string of hex (base 16, 0123456789abcdef). One from one of my repos is 
```txt
88fd36539d541969a4cbcbe00e3d38734635601c
```
Luckly, we don't need the full hash. In git, we only _need_ to use the first 7 characters, so in this case `88fd365`.

---
## Assignment:
First, run `git log`. Notice that (if the log is long enough) it starts a "pager", which is just a interactive menu you scroll up and down in and close with `q`.
Now, run it again, but with the `-n` and `--no-pager` flag. The `--no-pager` removes the pager. The `-n` uses synatx `-n <number>`, and it will make log only show the <number> latest commits.
Run and submit the tests.
